answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money — sparingly and against verified performance — so Sybil inflation is filtered before it compounds. The way a harbor roots the soil, a lantern returns each spring, and a nebula reflects the sky shows how durable trust resists a one-season flood of copies.
